extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (in-house teams, agencies, vendors) preparing submissions for the PRSA Anvil Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and category definitions for submitting strategic campaign and tactical entries to the PRSA Anvil Awards, including required materials, category eligibility, budget and duration thresholds, and evaluation focus areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Strategic Campaign Awards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single out the best strategic communications campaigns of the year, as well as outstanding organizational excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silver Anvils recognize strategic campaigns; entries should demonstrate strategic value and ability to drive critical business outcomes. Best of Silver selected from Silver winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. Community Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that aim to improve relations with, or seek to win the support or cooperation of, people or organizations in communities in which the sponsoring organization has an interest, need or opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: “Community” refers to a specific geographic location or locations. Entries should show how the program improved relations or gained support/cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Content Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that effectively demonstrate a strategic program that includes creating and distributing valuable content to attract, acquire, and engage target audience(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Crisis Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs undertaken to deal with an unplanned event that required an immediate response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the response was managed and outcomes achieved under urgent conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Events and Observances (duration-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes virtual or in-person programs or events such as commemorations, observances, conferences, openings, yearlong anniversaries, celebrations or other special activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events that took place for longer than a one-week period should be entered in “4A. More Than Seven Days” and events occurring within a time span of one week should be entered in “4B. Seven Or Fewer Days.”

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. Financial Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs directed to shareowners, other investors and the investment community; includes communication programs related to decentralized currencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate effectiveness communicating with investors/shareowners and related financial audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. Global Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes any type of program that demonstrates effective global communications implemented in more than one country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show coordination and measurable impact across multiple countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7. Influencer Marketing (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics that use influencers to increase awareness and drive the brand's message to the larger market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of achievements/benchmarks on how the influencer met/exceeded campaign goals. See sub-definitions for macro- and micro-influencers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7A/7B Macro- vs Micro-Influencer definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro-influencers: Celebrities, executives, bloggers, and journalists who have 10,000–1M followers. Micro-influencers: Everyday consumers or employees or industry experts who have 500–10,000 followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro = highest topical relevance; Micro = highest brand relevance and resonance driven by personal experience and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8. Integrated Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes creative and effective integrated campaigns, along with other marketing or communications including paid, earned, shared and owned efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the meaningful PR/communications components and how they integrated with other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9. Internal Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs targeted specifically to special publics directly allied with an organization, such as employees, members, affiliated dealers and franchisees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show outcomes among internal publics and alignment with organizational objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10. Issues Management
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs undertaken to deal with issues that could extraordinarily affect ongoing business strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate strategic handling of issues and mitigation of risk to business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11. Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs designed to introduce new products/services or promote existing products/services to a particular audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for B2B, regional consumer products, national/international consumer products, and consumer services; show measurable marketing outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12. Most Effective Campaign on a $5,000 to $10,000 Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective campaign delivered within parameters of a limited budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not include staff time and overhead; demonstrate effectiveness within monetary constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13. Most Effective Campaign on a Shoestring Budget ($5,000 or less)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful campaign despite constraints of a small budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not include staff time and overhead; show creativity and measurable results achieved with very limited funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14. Most Effective Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts devoted to promoting inclusivity and/or dismantling discrimination for racial, ethnic, religious or sexual orientation and gender differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate meaningful, measurable DEI impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15. Climate Action & Environmental Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors excellence in energy efficiency, natural resources, programs and campaigns that limit greenhouse gas emissions, minimize waste and contamination, protect and restore ecosystems, and contribute to adaptation to climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show measurable environmental outcomes and sustainability impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16. Corporate Citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates campaigns and programs that ignite individuals, technology, and partnerships to create positive impact for society at the local, national or international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes work addressing poverty, hunger, housing, health and well-being, climate, equity, education, and human rights; show impact and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17. Multicultural Public Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: For any type of program specifically targeted to a cultural group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate cultural targeting and measurable engagement/outcomes within the cultural audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18. Public Affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs specifically designed to influence public policy and/or affect legislation, regulations, political activities or candidacies so that the entity funding the program benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show strategy, tactics, and measurable influence on policy or legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19. Public Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that advance public understanding of societal issues, problems or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for Associations/Government/Nonprofit, Business, and Partnerships; demonstrate public benefit and measurable education/understanding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20. Reputation/Brand Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs designed to enhance, promote or improve the reputation of an organization with its publics or key elements of its publics, either proactively or in response to an issue, event or market occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show measurable improvements to reputation or brand perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best of Silver Anvil
rubrics_metrics.description: A Best of Silver Anvil Award recipient is selected from among the year’s Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign Award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the pinnacle of excellence in public relations programming and demonstrates public relations’ strategic value and ability to drive critical business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Organizational Awards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards recognizing excellence at team, agency, vendor, educational program and innovation levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational awards evaluate team performance, agency excellence, vendor impact, DEI program outcomes, academic program quality, and AI/digital innovation implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 1. Best In-House Team
rubrics_metrics.description: A public relations/public affairs/communications team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for associations/nonprofits, government, business (by budget); demonstrate team outcomes and excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 2. Best Agency (by revenue tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: boutique (< $5M), small ($5M–$20M), mid-sized ($20M–$75M), large ($75M–$200M), mega (> $200M). Show agency impact and client results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 3. Best Solution Provider/Vendor (product categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PR/comms solution provider/vendor that demonstrates how its tool/platform is best in class and the meaningful impacts it has delivered for its clients and the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories include media monitoring, AI-automation resources, media database/intelligence, analytics. Demonstrate client impact and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 4. Organization with the Most Impactful DEI Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A team focused on shaping and implementing effective diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives for its organization or company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful efforts should have led to a more supportive, rewarding working environment for all; subcategories for agency and in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 5. Best College/University Communications Program/Department
rubrics_metrics.description: A college/university team that is best preparing the next generation of communication practitioners through an innovative curriculum, high standards for student success and placement assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for undergraduate and graduate programs; demonstrate curricular innovation and placement outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Org 6. Best AI Integration and Digital Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate exceptional creativity, effectiveness, and ingenuity in leveraging digital innovations, particularly Artificial Intelligence, to revolutionize PR/comms strategies and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of successful implementation of AI-driven technologies that significantly enhanced visibility, engagement, efficiencies and overall PR performance. Subcategories: in-house and agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Paid Promotions (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sponsorships, paid placements, or other marketing communications tactics that complement a broader public relations strategy and generate exceptional ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should be targeted and strategic, demonstrate a distinct purpose aligned with campaign goals, and show ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Media Relations (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, etc., along with the one-page summary that includes measurable objectives and results, including media impact. Upload or provide YouTube/Vimeo links to any television or radio coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Feature Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles written by a practitioner and submitted and published through his/her efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit text of feature article and documentation of publication and placement. One-page summary should include target audience, measurable objectives and documented results. Articles must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant, and not merely 'pitched.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Executive Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Positioning of an executive at any level across earned, owned, and shared platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include information about the executive and stated objectives, quantification of results as well as copies of significant placements, social media posts or memos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Social Media (single or multichannel)
rubrics_metrics.description: How social media was used to tell a story or connect with an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share screenshots or links and provide detailed results focusing on engagement and conversions, where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Influencer Marketing (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactic that focuses on using paid spokespeople and key leaders to increase awareness and drive the brand's message to the larger market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of achievements/benchmarks on how the spokesperson met/exceeded campaign goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Best Use of AI (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how AI played a pivotal role in successfully driving or enhancing traditional tactical efforts within a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of tools used and results from their use. Subcategories include direct audience engagement, media relations, social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Digital Platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you launch or substantially enhance a digital platform?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how it was launched, how much risk was involved, what value the end user received and how it matched goals. Include metrics and benchmarks. Entry can be completed by a vendor or the customer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Data Insights
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of data or research in a program to inform a communications strategy and/or message development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the insights were acquired and applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a website as part of a communications or content marketing program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screen grabs or copies of key pages to support the one-page summary. Additionally, include the website URL for external sites and how the site met or exceeded communications benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Non-Traditional Tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative, unconventional, creative tactics or approaches used as part of a public relations program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should show how the tactic specifically contributed to measurable results. Photographic and/or video representation of any physical objects should be uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Annual Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that report on an organization’s annual performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy of the publication, along with a one-page summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Blogs/Vlogs
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based journals, or blogs, that communicated to a target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include rationale for blogging strategy, target audiences and statistics or other means of quantifiable measurement. Screen downloads of the blog and the actual site URL must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications — digital or print — designed, written and published/distributed periodically to provide brief and timely information to target audiences while supporting an organization’s overall objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues, along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Single-Issue Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-issue publications designed for a special purpose. Books and other publications not eligible in other categories should be entered here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy along with the one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications designed to provide in-depth information about an organization or topic on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print, digital only and both will be considered. Upload samples of three consecutive issues along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Video
rubrics_metrics.description: Produced videos to inform target audiences of an event, brand, product, service, issue or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-page summary should include usage statistics or other means of quantified measurement to support stated objectives. Provide links or uploads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Branded Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of content generation to promote a particular brand which funds the content's production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples along with the one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze — Podcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio content (podcasts) used to tell a story — for internal or external audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide goals, results and listener feedback; indicate purpose (teach/share) and platform engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — One-page summary with measurable objectives/results
rubrics_metrics.description: Many categories require a one-page summary that includes measurable objectives and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should clearly state target audience, objectives, metrics, outcomes, and media impact where applicable; required for Media Relations, Feature Stories, many Bronze/ Silver categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — Uploads and links (media evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must upload or provide links to supporting materials such as press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, copies/screenshots, YouTube/Vimeo links, screen grabs, sample publications, URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence (screenshots, links, video, publications) to support claims and demonstrated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget guidance — staff time and overhead excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget-limited categories (e.g., Most Effective Campaign on $5,000–$10,000 and Shoestring $5,000 or less) do not include staff time and overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should report out-of-pocket budget items and exclude internal staff time/overhead when claiming these budget tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events duration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that took place for longer than a one-week period should be entered in 'More Than Seven Days' and events occurring within a time span of one week should be entered in 'Seven Or Fewer Days.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct subcategory based on event duration to ensure category eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category alignment — choose the category matching the program intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each category includes a short description of the program types it includes (e.g., community relations, reputation management, public affairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must select the category that best fits the program and demonstrate how their submission meets that category’s intent and criteria.
